customManagers.description: The Kubernetes version the Omni cluster template installs. Applying a bump reboots every machine, so it is never automerged (see the omni/** rule).
The Talos version the machines run. Same reboot, and Omni upgrades one minor at a time with irreversible database migrations behind it.

The Cilium version generate.sh renders cilium-install.yaml from. That generated file is never edited by Renovate - it would be undone by the next ./generate.sh - so this is the only place the version exists.
The Flux install manifests the one-time bootstrap applies. The running controllers come from these, so a bump is applied by hand with kubectl apply -k.

The vendored Traefik CRD bundle, which has to move with the traefik image in network/traefik/base/deployment.yaml - they were allowed to drift once, and newer fields were silently pruned. Never automerged (see the vendored-files rule).

The kubectl the validation workflows install. It is deliberately not tied to the cluster's Kubernetes version: kubectl supports one minor either side, so this is a bump to review rather than to follow blindly.
yamllint, pinned with == in the validation workflows. A linter bump can change what passes, so it lands as a pull request.
kubeconform, downloaded by version in the validation workflows.

packageRules.description: Automerge the small stuff (digest, pin, patch) with no human in the loop - a version bump inside the same release line. platformAutomerge stays false on purpose: with it on, GitHub merges as soon as the repository's *required* checks pass, and this repository deliberately has none - so a bump would land before the validation that .github/workflows/validate-renovate.yaml runs. With it off, Renovate itself merges on a later run, once the branch carries a green renovate/validate status.

Minor updates are not automerged: for the charts this cluster runs (longhorn, metallb, cert-manager, oauth2-proxy) a minor bump changes defaults and upgrades running components, and the validation these branches get is shape-only - it renders and lints, it does not exercise a volume or a webhook. They wait as pull requests. To automate them too, add "minor" to the matchUpdateTypes above.
Major updates change defaults and are read by a human, always. Errors and alerts from these changes are not something the cluster should discover on its own.

The cluster's own definition: the Omni template (Talos, Kubernetes) and the Cilium version generate.sh renders from. Never automerged, whatever the update type - applying one reboots every machine, Omni upgrades one minor at a time, and the Cilium manifest has to be regenerated and synced by hand afterwards.
CI tooling is a bump to read, not one to follow the cluster with: yamllint, kubeconform and the kubectl the workflows install all change what a green check means.
The vendored Traefik CRD bundle has to move with the traefik image in network/traefik/base/deployment.yaml - it is pinned by hand to the release the binary runs - so never automerge a bump inside it.
